channel.title: World News
channel.description: Aggregated headlines linking to original publishers

item.title: Protesters against gender-based violence denounce 149 femicides in France
item.description: Protesters against gender-based violence took to the streets of Paris on Saturday, flooding the capital with banners that denounced, among other things, the 149 reported femicides that took place in France this year. FRANCE 24 journalist Caroline Baum brings us more from the site ofthe demonstration.

item.title: What to know about the weather-delayed 100th Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade
item.description: The 100th annual Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade will take place Saturday morning.

item.title: WWE star Bronson Reed dies at 38 due to 'medical complications'
item.description: Jermaine Haley, the WWE star known as Bronson Reed, has died at 38 due to "medical complications," the company announced on Friday.

item.title: Taipei's Kuomintang mayor Chiang Wan-an re-elected in tight election race
item.description: Taipei Mayor Chiang Wan-an was re-elected on Saturday after a nail-biting race against China critic Puma Shen in local elections held across the island democracy.

item.title: Gaza strike kills two Doctors Without Borders staff Israel links to Hamas
item.description: Doctors Without Borders (MSF) voiced outrage on Saturday after an Israeli strike killed two staff members at a clinic in Gaza, while the Israeli military said the pair were Hamas "terrorists". The Friday night strike in Gaza City drew swift condemnation from the head of the UN's World Health Organization and came despite a ceasefire in the war-shattered Palestinian territory.

item.title: COP31 climate talks fail to reach an agreement on fossil fuel language
item.description: U.N. climate talks collapsed over whether to mention fossil fuels that cause global warning. Several countries and the E.U. would not accept a final proposal without this.

item.title: Man arrested at airport over death of 16-year-old girl
item.description: A man has been arrested on suspicion of murdering a 16-year-old girl in east London.

item.title: France holds nationwide protests against violence towards women
item.description: Demonstrations condemning violence against women are drew thousands across France on Saturday, with feminist organisations, labour unions, students and Yellow Vest activists taking part. The marches come amid a broader wave of social unrest, with cost-of-living protests entering their seventh consecutive week.

item.title: Israeli strike on Gaza kills two medics from Doctors Without Borders
item.description: An Israeli strike killed two doctors who were working members of Doctors Without Borders in Gaza City on Friday night, drawing widespread condemnation, including from the UN's World Health Organization. Israeli military claims the pair were Hamas "terrorists".

item.title: Perspective: A hero's name lives on
item.description: During Pearl Harbor, sailor Doris Miller carried the wounded to safety and fired a machine gun at Japanese planes. Next week, construction of a new aircraft carrier, the USS Doris Miller, begins.

item.title: Marches planned in France amid alarming global statistics on women’s safety
item.description: Cynthia Illouz, founder of French-American News media @thewomensvoices, is our guest.

item.title: Credit rating agency S&P may downgrade France's credit rating
item.description: Credit rating agency S&P on Friday maintained France's A+ credit rating but lowered its outlook for the country to negative from stable, warning of a possible downgrade as the country struggles to bring down its budget deficit.

item.title: WATCH: 'Ugly pants exchange' trend goes viral among air travelers
item.description: A new viral trend at airports has emerged among groups of friends traveling together: bringing extra pairs of pants along for a lighthearted swap and reveal.

item.title: Heavy rain, gale force winds and flooding forecast for UK
item.description: Warnings have been issued for heavy rain, gale force winds and possible flooding across parts of the UK from Monday.

item.title: An explosion at a school in eastern Afghanistan kills 10, wounds 110
item.description: Local officials said the blast appeared to have originated in a neighboring depot for mining explosives.

item.title: Police arrest 33 people in child sexual exploitation investigation
item.description: Police investigating suspected child sexual exploitation involving "men who were in contact with teenage girls" in Southampton have made dozens of arrests.

item.title: Israeli strike kills two Doctors Without Borders staff in Gaza
item.description: Doctors Without Borders (MSF) said Saturday an Israeli strike killed two staff members at a clinic in Gaza, with the Israeli army labelling the pair as Hamas "terrorists". Noga Tarnopolsky is live from Jerusalem.

item.title: Three days in the dark: How prepared are we for the lights to go out?
item.description: Authorities are urging households to prepare for 72 hours without power, water or internet access as cyberattacks, infrastructure failures and extreme weather expose France and other countries to national security vulnerabilities. The message is of practical resilience, not alarm: modest preparations can help keep people safe when essential services falter – and recent security breaches are sparking a wider reckoning across Europe, including France's presidential campaigns.

item.title: Taiwan holds elections to choose mayors and other local leaders
item.description: Jan Camenzind Broomby is live from Taipei, Taiwan.

item.title: Europe prepares for a very cold winter as temperatures are expected to drop
item.description: Daniela Domeisen, associate professor at the University of Lausanne, is our guest.

item.title: Outbreak of diarrhea amongst young children in Gabon, Africa
item.description: In the Gabonese capital, many babies are being admitted to hospitals in a state of dehydration due to diarrhea. The cause: treatment that is often delayed and inadequate.

item.title: More children reunited with their families amid war in Ukraine
item.description: Nine ​additional ​children have been reunited with ​their ‌families ⁠amid ‌the war ⁠in Ukraine, bringing the ​total to ‌43 amid an ‌effort ​led by US first lady Melania ​Trump, ​the ​White House ​said on Wednesday.

item.title: War in the Middle East: Surge of violence in occupied West Bank
item.description: The four Israeli soldiers stepped out of their car in the occupied West Bank, their faces masked, their uniforms unmarked and automatic weapons strapped across their shoulders. They had entered a Palestinian olive grove but, little did they expect, the person there planning to tell them to leave could have once been issuing them orders.

item.title: Taiwan awaits local election results as China watches
item.description: Taipei Mayor ​Chiang Wan-an ​is leading in the vote count in ​an ‌election ⁠against his opponent Puma ‌Shen, Taiwan media outlets ⁠reported on Saturday.

item.title: Syrian Kurds protest against Baghdad leader's moves to assert central control
item.description: Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi is taking bold steps to curb rampant oil smuggling, moves that the US has praised but that risk putting him at odds with Iraq's Kurds and neighbouring Iran.

item.title: What are the main issues driving Spain's national election ?
item.description: Spain will elect a new government on Sunday in a snap election that could unseat Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez. The progressive leader has governed Spain for 8 years, presiding over several crises, years of economic expansion and immigration-led population growth. No issue, however, has affected Spaniards during this time as much as unaffordable housing.

item.title: World Health Organization sounds alarm as measles fight stalls
item.description: Global measles deaths hit a historic low in 2025, the World Health Organization said on Friday, although millions of children ⁠still missed vaccinations and outbreaks persisted in dozens of countries. The UN health agency estimated 9.8 million measles cases and about 72,000 deaths worldwide in 2025 — down 74% from 37.8 million cases in 2000, with deaths falling roughly 91% from about 769,000.

item.title: Explosion at a school in eastern Afghanistan kills 7, wounds more than 90
item.description: An explosion at a school in eastern Afghanistan's Kunar province Saturday killed seven people and wounded over 90

item.title: Immigration, a key issue in Sunday's Spanish snap election
item.description: Vox has focused its campaign on immigration, which dominated politics after tens of thousands of migrants streamed into Spain's north African city of Ceuta from Morocco in July.

item.title: Italy issues warning to Zelenskyy after Ukrainian attack on Russian ships in Libya
item.description: The Italian prime minister has warned Ukraine not to allow its conflict with Russia to spill over into the Mediterranean after Kyiv attacked two Russian ships in Libya.

item.title: New wave of Democratic attorneys general may reshape the justice system
item.description: The Democratic victories could have major effects for what alleged crimes are investigated, lawsuits filed and court cases heard across the U.S.

item.title: Live: Ukraine downs Russian drone with laser technology as Moscow intercepts overnight assault
item.description: Russia shot down over 1,200 drones targeting Moscow overnight, Russian authorities said Saturday. Both Russia and Ukraine have stepped up their attacks using projectiles in recent months, with Ukraine confirming on Friday it had downed a Russian jet-powered drone with laser technology for the first time. Follow our liveblog for the latest updates.

item.title: Captain Tom charity applies to be struck off following family misconduct
item.description: The charity set up by the family of pandemic fundraiser Captain Sir Tom Moore has applied to be struck off.

item.title: Taiwan mayoral candidate criticised by Beijing concedes defeat
item.description: Taiwan’s ruling Democratic Progressive Party suffered a setback in Saturday’s local elections, conceding defeat in Taipei and preserving the opposition's hold on the capital. The elections across the island’s 22 cities and counties focused largely on local concerns, though tensions with Beijing remained in the background.

item.title: Hackers reportedly breach US Air Force cloud platform as Pentagon insists systems are secure
item.description: Hackers reportedly breached the US Air Force's Cloud One platform late Friday, potentially exposing sensitive military data. The Pentagon did not specifically deny that the system had been accessed, but insists its networks remain secure amid an ongoing spate of cyber-related data incidents.

item.title: Children urged to get flu vaccine after 'horrible spike' in cases
item.description: Thousands of children who missed their flu vaccine in school can get one at a pharmacy for the first time.

item.title: Doctors Without Borders 'outraged' after staff killed in Gaza
item.description: A humanitarian medical charity says it is "devastated and outraged" after two civil guards at one of its offices in Gaza were killed in an Israeli strike.

item.title: UK makes demand to Argentina after court rejects Milei's bid to block Falklands oil project
item.description: Argentina's president has claimed the Falklands "are Argentine" after an international court rejected his bid to block oil drilling off the disputed islands.

item.title: Woman, 21, dies after crash following police pursuit
item.description: A 21-year-old woman has died after a crash following a police pursuit - with the actions of two police forces prior to the collision under investigation.

item.description: New York state Senate Majority Leader Andrea Stewart-Cousins has died

item.description: Andscape senior entertainment reporter Kelley Carter discusses what defines a classic holiday film, shares her top picks and weighs in on if "Die Hard" qualifies as a holiday movie.

item.title: Sales for Biden memoir fall far short of books by Obama, Clinton
item.description: Former President Joe Biden’s memoir “Promise Me, America” has sold around 21,000 copies during its first week on sale, according to Circana, a firm which tracks the physical book sales market

item.title: French cinema star Gérard Depardieu ordered to stand trial for rape and sexual assault
item.description: The case has become one of the most prominent in France's reckoning with sexual violence, as the #MeToo movement has faced resistance in the country, particularly in the arts.

item.title: WATCH: 12-year-old soccer star turns hearing loss into inspiration
item.description: ABC News' Danny New has the story of Delaney Anbardan, a young soccer player in Southern California who has continued pursuing the sport while navigating progressive hearing loss.

item.title: From Thanksgiving blackouts to Black Friday, a holiday hit by wild weather and economic woes
item.description: A storm battered much of the country on Thursday, knocking out power to thousands of homes and disrupting travel. Today, Black Friday shopping deals kick off, and on Saturday New York City will hold the postponed Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade.

item.title: Can luxury save Macy's?
item.description: This week's celebration of Macy's 100th Thanksgiving parade finds the department store at a turning point. After years of losing sales, the retailer is reimagining itself — as a higher-end destination.

item.title: Trump effectively ended asylum. Advocates look to the Supreme Court to restore it
item.description: Trump's sweeping immigration changes — an asylum ban, mass firings and new legal maneuvers — have all but ended asylum. The high court will soon consider whether some shifts deny people due process.

item.description: Amazon employees around the world are set to stage protests on Black Friday amid claims of unfair pay and oppressive working conditions.

item.description: ABC News' Michelle Franzen takes us to Plymouth, Massachusetts, where the tradition of Thanksgiving began when English settlers shared a meal with native tribes.

item.title: WATCH: Viral Thanksgiving story set to be adapted for small screen
item.description: Jamal Hinton and Wanda Dench's viral story of a wrong text that led to a decadelong Thanksgiving tradition is set to become a Lifetime production. Will Ganss shares the buzziest stories in Pop News.

item.title: Driver suspected of causing tanker crash in Egypt that killed 31 detained
item.description: The driver of a car suspected to have caused a fuel tanker to overturn in Egypt, causing the deaths of 31 people, has been detained.

item.title: Witnesses contacted as US probe into World Cup sell-off plan intensifies
item.description: A planned US congressional investigation into FIFA and Gianni Infantino's World Cup sell-off plans is intensifying with requests to speak to current and former FIFA staff, Sky News understands.

item.description: In the latest on the ongoing manhole mystery in New York City, the NYPD has released new images of suspects seen exiting a manhole last week.

item.title: WATCH: Women around the world fight for gender equity in sumo
item.description: For more than 1,500 years, professional sumo has only allowed men into the ring. Nightline traveled to Japan to learn more about the ancient ban and meet with athletes fighting against tradition.

item.description: ABC News' Danny New talks to a doctor in New York who's using his balloon twisting talents to help him pay off his student loan debt.

item.description: Nutrition specialist J.J. Virgin and etiquette expert Thomas Farley discuss how you can navigate some of Thanksgiving's tricky problems.

item.title: They want to watch Fort Hood shooter Nidal Hasan die but the Army won’t let them
item.description: Julia Wilson was nine months pregnant when she found herself caught in gunfire at Fort Hood in 2009. 'It's crazy how quickly things run through your brain," she said.
